title: How do we divide a fraction by a fraction?
description: One fifth divided by one half is turned into a multiplication with a missing number. First a product of one is made, then it is changed to one fifth. Keeko raises the doubt of just multiplying the two fractions.
teaching_notes: One idea: to divide by a fraction, first make a product of one, then change it to the number we want. Watch for students who multiply the two fractions as they are and get a smaller number.

video_script.why: A learner sees how a fraction divided by a fraction becomes a multiplication with a missing number, built in two small steps.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own fraction by fraction division, one fifth and one half
video_script.anchor: one fifth divided by one half written beside one half times a missing number equals one fifth
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the two fractions as they are instead of dividing
video_script.payoff_line: One fifth divided by one half is two fifths
video_script.fraction_reading: one fifth, one half, two fifths, one tenth, one twentieth
video_script.design: A division and a multiplication with a missing number, joined by a double arrow. The product of one is built first and then changed to one fifth.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the division 1/5 ÷ 1/2 on the board

marks.pose: the division arrives on the board
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the division

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about dividing a fraction by a fraction.
<bookmark mark='pose'/>Find one fifth divided by one half, by asking what number times one half gives one fifth.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is one fifth divided by one half?

beats.on_screen: the division stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: 1/5 ÷ 1/2 = ? beside 1/2 × ? = 1/5, joined by a double arrow

marks.link: the division and the multiplication are joined by a double arrow
marks.plan: a path is drawn from the divisor to one, and then from one to the dividend

narration: <bookmark mark='link'/>Every division can be turned into a multiplication with a missing number.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>We can first reach one, and then change one into the number we want.

marks.given: the two fractions are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fractions are one fifth and one half.

marks.find: the words To find and the division are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find one fifth divided by one half.

marks.write: the division is rewritten as a multiplication with a missing number

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write the division as a multiplication, one half times what is one fifth?
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, one half times two is one, so we multiply by two first.

marks.fifth: a times one fifth is added to the product of one

narration: <bookmark mark='fifth'/>Step three, we want one fifth, so also multiply by one fifth.

marks.miss: the missing number is read off the product
marks.mult: the tops are multiplied over the bottom

narration: <bookmark mark='miss'/>Step four, the missing number is two times one fifth.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>That is two times one on top, over five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>One fifth divided by one half is two fifths.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 1/5 × 1/2 = 1/10; the check 1/10 × 1/2 = 1/20 is written beside it and crossed

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the two fractions multiplied
marks.slip: the check is written and the result one twentieth is crossed
marks.fix: the missing number is changed to a times two

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we multiply the two fractions, so the answer is one tenth.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But one tenth times one half is one twentieth, not one fifth.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>We must multiply by two, the number that makes one half into one.
